title: GS21 U-shaped exposure (0.28, 0, 0, 0, 0.28) across a MILD visible level ladder 0.8..1.2 (gs_level), five types, exact compensation, price 2.5 (small firms constrained, large firms operationally levered)
question: Does a U-shaped loading across size give GS21 room and a fair gap at the bar?
notes:
WHY (2026-11-01). A non-monotone exposure with a simple story, built the same way in every model: five equal types on the mild visible level ladder 0.8..1.2 with the loading U-shaped across it, b = (0.28, 0, 0, 0, 0.28), exact y = 0 compensation (bv_comp 1.0) so that only size carries the U. Small firms are exposed to the aggregate cash-flow shock through financing constraints, large firms through operating leverage, mid-sized firms through neither. The hump twins (bvyhx4 / vyhx4 / gvyhx4, b = -c, 0, +c, 0, -c) are running; the U has no sign flip and all its exposure is of one sign, so its mean is not zero and the market holds the common part; the room is the curvature in size, which no linear function of the characteristics spans (bvyvee's V across the WIDE ladder 0.6..1.4 failed because the level's own monotone premium swamped it; the mild ladder and the larger loading are bvyhx3/4's fix).

PRECOMMITMENT STATUS: precommitted=false; ids filled from the Quest build log by the solve script before any seed runs.

PREDICTION (2026-11-01): premium U-shaped in size; oracle room 30% or more and a fair gap at or above +0.029 in BGN (bvyhx4 gave +0.119 with the sign flip); KP14 and GS21 as their hump twins. FALSIFIED if room is at or below 15% on three seeds.

method.gs_ashift_ladder: derived: -bv_comp log W(gs_bv), applied in solver and simulator
method.gs_vy_sign_ladder: U-shaped gs_bv across the visible gs_level ladder, each type level-compensated at y = 0 (bv_comp 1.0)
method.gs_level_ladder: explicit per-type production-level multiplier gs_level, log gs_level added to the production exponent beside gs_ashift in solver and simulator (read per type from each solution)

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks (global numpy stream) and the AGGREGATE state path (gam_seed / bx_seed / reg_seed offset by the seed). Seed 0 reproduces the single-run behaviour; --common_aggregate restores the fixed-aggregate behaviour as an explicit variance decomposition.
